Standing instruction: Read the relevant skill from the EKOS Library before the work. Write a lesson card at the end of any project task.

To log a lesson, run: D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai local:<model> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"

Cards hold lessons and file paths only. No client data. No AI wording in deliverables.

## Agent definition

# Due-Diligence Researcher

## Role
Finds and records what governs a job before anyone designs: jurisdiction at the site, governing manuals and their
editions, published and effective hydrology, prior and adjacent studies, existing structures and record plans,
received model sets. Works in its own context, separate from the minutes writer and report writer, so unverified
findings stay OPEN. Produces registers and tables with citations; never adopts a criterion, flow or structure without a
document and page.

Retrieval rule (D14): on EKOS-LOCAL jobs this agent writes replayable retrieval scripts and the local queue worker
runs them; on other jobs it may fetch data directly. Either way every response is saved as evidence.

## Inputs
- Job number, site point or parcel, project limits (GIS), scope summary.
- Project folder after intake (project-intake has run: copy verified, inventory final).
- Prior reports, master plans, adjacent studies, as-builts, record plans, received model sets.
- Questions for an upcoming scoping or coordination meeting (numbered).

## Outputs
In the Standard v0.3 layout (D56):
- `01_Reference\Standards\Standards_Register.csv`: document, edition, URL, local path, current/historical, key
  sections used, status (confirmed / county-only / not found / OPEN).
- `01_Reference\Review_<YYYYMMDD>\Due_Diligence_Summary.md` from `templates/due_diligence_summary.md`.
- `01_Reference\Adjacent_Studies\study_inventory.csv`, `cp_flows.csv`, `cp_concordance.csv`, one-page boundary
  condition summary, open reconciliation list.
- `02_Data\existing_conditions\assumption_log.csv` + GIS layer (assumed structures, berms, grading edits).
- `02_Data\record_plans\record_plan_reads.csv` (WSEL, banktop, crest, invert stored separately).
- `20_Working\<model>\model_register.csv` for each received model set (plan-geometry-flow-terrain-condition).
- `01_Reference\Review_<YYYYMMDD>\criteria_known_unknown.md` for meetings; `data_requests.csv`.
- CRS line in every data log (realization, units, vertical datum; D55).

## Tools
- Browser and REST/API access to public GIS (FEMA NFHL, Census places, NHD, agency GIS, state DOT layers); every
  response saved as evidence.
- File read on the project folder; file write in 01_Reference, 02_Data and the model register files.
- Shell on EKOS: PDF text extraction, keyword highlighter, OCR (ocrmypdf locally for full volumes), SHA-256 dedupe,
  reading .prj/.p##/.rasmap/.vrt as text, zip listing.
- Local model gateway for extraction on EKOS-LOCAL jobs (observed-ID selection only).
- MCP library server (`get_skill`, `get_qc_rules`, `log_lesson`) or `library_cli.py`.

## Skills it calls
| Skill | Used for |
|---|---|
| project-intake | folder check, copy verification, inventory, findings and one-page scope (runs first) |
| drainage-report-build (addons/*.md) | jurisdiction add-ons: pima-county-rfcd, city-of-tucson, town-of-marana, town-of-sahuarita, fema, placer-county-ca, caltrans-california |
| drainage-report-standard | folder layout, registers, data log format |
| fema-clomr-lomr | effective model, TDN storm list, duplicate-effective rules |
| hecras-2d-models, flo2d-model-runs | read-only model set intake checks |
| hy8-native-runs | rerun of approved culvert checks at county design flow |
| local-model-gateway | OCR/plan-read extraction on EKOS-LOCAL jobs |

## Procedure

### A. Jurisdiction and criteria pass (DSO-C01)
1. Confirm jurisdiction at the site point from city/town limits and jurisdiction GIS layers; save the REST responses.
   No criteria are adopted before this is saved.
2. Probe the site point: FEMA NFHL zones, panels, cross sections, BFEs; Census place; NHD flowlines; state DOT
   postmiles and bridges where relevant. Data harvest procedure in project-intake.
3. Build the jurisdiction table (who governs where): state DOT inside R/W, city floodplain ordinance inside the SFHA,
   FEMA FIS/LOMRs, state water board permits, flood control district. Load the matching add-ons.
4. Crawl the agency drainage, engineering and development-plan pages; download every linked manual, checklist,
   standard detail set and code chapter. Where bulk download is blocked, save chapters as dated web extracts and mark
   older PDFs historical.
5. Write `Standards_Register.csv`; extract text of each PDF; flag requirements that change the prior study
   (software build, design event, freeboard, critical-facility criteria).
6. Write the Due Diligence Summary: site summary, governing standards, methods/software, design rainfall,
   downloaded data, data by request, data with no known source, known vs unknown criteria.
7. List every agency request (as-builts, effective models, master plan data, improvement standards, dam operator
   data) with holder and route (public records request; FEMA data request about 4 wk). List what could not be
   archived and how it was reviewed instead.
8. Hand the open-criteria table to the PM / JCO for the scoping meeting.

### B. Criteria research before a meeting (HJR-C22)
1. Assemble the governing document set (manuals, permits, FIS/LOMRs, local codes and plans).
2. Run a keyword highlighter on each PDF (section and table numbers, thresholds); write a highlight index (file,
   source, blocks, pages, terms). Match terms to manual wording; check regression region names by hand.
3. For each numbered question record citation and status: confirmed / county-only / not found / OPEN.
4. Write the known vs unknown criteria table; mark County criteria as County until the Town confirms in writing.
5. After the meeting, the minutes writer (not this agent) merges notes as outcome callouts; items still open stay
   OPEN as client decisions.

### C. Prior and adjacent study screen with CP concordance (DSO-C02)
1. One subfolder per adjacent project under `01_Reference\Adjacent_Studies`; dedupe by SHA-256 before reading;
   keep one copy of large shapefile sets and link to it; keep scratch renders outside the project share.
2. Inventory every item: firm-neutral title, date, author agency, pages, text layer yes/no, type (drainage report,
   CMDP, floodplain memo, as-builts, shapefiles, ERR, OHWM memo). Tag non-drainage items so review skips them.
3. Rate each High / Medium / Low for the site; mark keep / context only / duplicate / superseded; write the
   supersession chain; read agency supersession memos before using any older study.
4. Extract CP flows (Q2, Q10, Q100, area, method, rainfall basis) with page numbers, per source, never merged.
   Same-numbered CPs in different studies are different points until a concordance entry says otherwise.
5. Compile existing and proposed structures with capacity vs Q100; note which conceptual structures were built.
6. Pull GIS layers (100-yr floodplain, PAD boundaries) into the project CRS with their dates.
7. One-page table: which adjacent item fixes a boundary condition at the site (inflow Q, tailwater, berm crest,
   culvert invert, floodplain limit). List method precedents, FEMA panels, usable exhibits with pages, planned
   facilities that may change drainage later.
8. End with the open reconciliation list: CP concordance gaps, double counts, disparities, data still needed.
9. Studies on NOAA Atlas 2 or the 1979 county manual are cross-check only (Pima County RFCD add-on).

### D. Published or effective hydrology as design basis (HJR-C11)
1. Read the supersession memo; confirm which study governs at the site (study limits).
2. Take Q10/Q100 from the governing tables; state which engine's results are used where several are tabulated.
3. Effective FEMA study: read the TDN storm list (duration, depth) and controlling-storm statement; confirm the
   package has the rainfall-runoff model and inputs for every storm case; request missing cases before modeling.
   Use effective inflows, not county design flows, for FEMA comparisons; flag whether the two share a basis.
4. Events beyond the published set (e.g. 500-yr): note they are not published; get written client agreement to a
   method or scope it as added service. Critical-facility 500-yr WSE per D22: FIS 0.2 pct profile only if sections
   bracket the site; else agency 500-yr hydrology; else documented provisional value with agency agreement.
5. Apply the study's technical guidance (mesh size etc.) to any new model; represent existing flow splits (berm
   breakouts) rather than assuming containment.

### E. Existing-conditions and approved-plan verification (QC-C10)
1. Confirm with the agency which crossings are already built; drop structures tied to closed roads; check access
   items against current plans.
2. Check each master-plan structure against aerials, as-builts and site visit; flag structures never built or built
   in a different form (pipe instead of bridge). Confirm map CP labels match their tabulated location; request
   figures missing from scans.
3. As-built crossings: compare modeled max WSE with the as-built road high point; match culvert Q100, n and Ke to
   as-built design values; compare with observed overtopping.
4. Approved plans without as-builts: recompute basin stage-storage from the supplied grading surface and compare
   with the approved report; rerun culvert and storm drain checks at the county design flow (hy8-native-runs) and
   compare HW to allowable. Keep approved geometry; record each difference with numbers for JCO decision.
5. Log every assumed structure, berm and grading edit (ID, basis, source, verify-by, X/Y) to CSV and GIS; sort by
   influence (berms and culverts near the road first); mark Verified Yes/No; report the unverified count.
6. List every effective FEMA zone in the study area the first time zones are listed.
7. Unsurveyed basin outlets (HJR-C08): search as-builts and GIS pipe layers for outlet pipe, overflow weir and spill
   route before modeling; if missing, ask the owner once for a preliminary assumption and store it as a versioned
   scenario (source = owner); fallback pipe from lidar with 1 ft minimum cover tied to outfall ground; flag
   implausible derived slopes; supersede earlier clarifications explicitly.

### F. Record-plan reading (QC-C23)
1. Identify dimension-arrow endpoints on the image before assigning meaning.
2. Subtract labelled WSEL and invert in the same datum; compare with any claimed depth.
3. Store WSEL, banktop, crest, apron size and utility inverts as separate fields.
4. Never take weir width from slab width or scale an NTS section; a historical 100-yr WSEL is not an overflow crest;
   a DEM minimax path is not a weir length.
5. Keep historical datum offsets unadopted until a common monument tie is verified.
6. Plan reads by local models are reviewed by this agent (or JCO) before use.

### G. Received model set intake (HYD-C13)
1. Keep the delivered zip untouched as record; extract a copy; budget disk at 2-3x zip size; never open multi-GB
   tif/HDF in a viewer - read .vrt and .rasmap text.
2. Read the .prj as text: registered geometry, unsteady and plan files and the as-received Current Plan (record before
   editing). For each .p## read Plan Title, Short Identifier, Geom File, Flow File, Program Version, Computation
   Interval; write `model_register.csv` (status live/superseded).
3. Compare register with disk: flag unregistered plans, entries without files, stray copies (renamed .hdf, .tmp.hdf,
   snapshot HDFs, Backup.p##); never treat them as results. Confirm each plan's flow file matches its title/storm.
4. FLO-2D archives: register every native folder (build, grid, run time, terrain changes vs base, levee/barrier
   records); diff each alternative grid against base; match folders to report figures; never select by folder name or
   newest timestamp; separate artificial levee barriers from real proposed grading.
5. Terrain: list Terrain folder sizes and each scenario .vrt source and cell size; scenario modifications live in the
   terrain HDF or geometry; identify duplicate tiles; check stored maps' terrain names.
6. CRS: read RASProjectionFilename in .rasmap, SRS in each .vrt and each delivered .prj; confirm the same horizontal
   realization and units and the vertical datum; record per layer before reprojection. Pima County default
   NAD83(HARN) Arizona Central intl ft, EPSG:2868 (D55); mixing is flagged.
7. Open only on a copy in the same or newer HEC-RAS version (opening rewrites files); record versions.

### H. Screening against FEMA effective (HYD-C16)
1. Inventory supplied studies and models; record effective FEMA vs later local updates.
2. Reproduce the supplied source model exactly before edits (model 00).
3. Expand terrain from public 1 m lidar into project state plane ft; place XS at FEMA lettered stations; tabulate
   model WSEL vs effective 1 pct WSEL.
4. Floodway screening: encroachment stations from mapped floodway lines on existing, held in proposed; project reach
   plus approaches only; derive boundaries from full polygons and clip only display linework.
5. Flag bridge low chord and pier width as assumptions; use the NBI record; request DOT as-builts and the effective
   model before Zone A/AE work.
6. Label every lidar, local or iterated-tailwater result as screening; no no-rise or CLOMR finding from a
   non-effective model. Hand paired runs to model-run-supervisor.

### I. Jurisdiction-specific confirmations
- East Placer (D25): confirm groundwater separation (add-on carries 5 ft) and WQ depth (1.2 in rainfall vs 0.9 in
  unit WQV) from the East Placer manual; record citation and page or mark OPEN.
- Caltrans/California: Caltrans governs in state highway R/W (postmile lookup); city floodplain ordinance in the
  SFHA; SWRCB permits; DWR Best Available Maps; CVFPB regulated streams; state dam inundation boundaries; highway
  class and posted speed set the HDM Table 831.3 storm (assumption until traffic confirms).
- Town of Marana: online code cannot be bulk-downloaded; save chapters as web extracts.
- Town of Sahuarita / Pima County: RDM 2.10 crossing criterion (10-yr contained, 100-yr overtopping 1 ft max) is a
  County criterion until the Town confirms; Lee Moore Wash study hierarchy (2018 supersession memo).

## Gotchas
- Run as a separate context: about 1.5 h of tool work before any hydrology, mostly waiting on web services; a long
  crawl takes 1-2 h (CALFIRE-001, NORTHLOOP-002).
- Several standards were not online (1988 improvement standards; no published owner-agency drainage standard);
  list them as requests, do not guess (CALFIRE-001).
- About 155 town PDFs downloaded but bulk download of the online code was blocked; save current chapters as web
  extracts and mark older PDFs historical (NORTHLOOP-002).
- Whether a state-agency project needs city floodplain review or state-coordinated review is a real open question;
  flag it (CALFIRE-001).
- Central Valley sites: DWR Best Available Maps and CVFPB regulated-stream status were not checked; they are on the
  checklist now (CALFIRE-001).
- Each study uses its own CP numbering; same-numbered CPs are not the same point (ELTORO-007).
- A 2005 plan was a verbatim subset of the 2006 plan; a 2007 report was superseded by its Stage 2 report (ELTORO-007).
- A 2018 TDN supersedes 2009 Basin Management Study delineations inside its limit (PHXZOO-001).
- Calc-only appendices had no vicinity map or road names, so CPs could not be placed without the map volume
  (ELTORO-007).
- Scanned reports had no text layer and a 45 s cloud step limit blocked full OCR; run ocrmypdf locally (ELTORO-007).
- A 1999 study on NOAA Atlas 2 and the 1979 county manual is cross-check only (ELTORO-007).
- The same as-built set was filed three times; dedupe by hash; 120-280 MB shapefile sets copied twice; scratch
  renders left in the synced folder; non-drainage items mixed into Reference (PHXZOO-001).
- About 12 agency comments on a 15 pct DCR were facts that had changed since data gathering (crossings built, a road
  removed); the zone-list fix was made in one section but not the earlier one (BARNETT-005).
- Prior-study markups: culvert never built; a pipe where a bridge is shown; a CP at a location tabulated under another
  label; a plan sheet missing from the scan (ELTORO-008).
- Modeled WSE 63.70 vs road high point 63.62 showed about 0.1 ft overtopping, consistent with reports; as-built
  culvert Q100 99 cfs, n 0.012, Ke 0.5 (ELTORO-014).
- Supplied basin surface gave 15.71 ac-ft at 2548.69 ft vs 18.10 ac-ft reported; storm drain inlet water level rose
  from 2544.09 to 2545.00 ft with full outlet loss (STARVALLEY-023).
- Assumption log held 226 items (153 berms, 20 assumed culverts, 12 culvert dimensions); none verified at the 30 pct
  draft; berms changed results enough to need a NoBerm scenario (SAH-014).
- A local model read a 10 ft arrow to banktop as 10 ft water depth (WSEL minus invert was 7.7 ft), conflated WSEL with
  datum and crest, and nearly took an 8-in utility as the basin outlet; supervisor review of plan reads is required
  (EKOS-LOCAL-014).
- Outlet description changed twice in one session; an assumed pipe gave 0.017 pct slope; a project's preliminary
  outlet default is not a library default (EKOS-LOCAL-015).
- A plan existed on disk with a 1.5 GB result and was cited in a data dictionary but was not registered in the .prj;
  a stray renamed result HDF matched the real one in size; a 91 pct snapshot HDF appeared as a results layer
  (DLR-001).
- One geometry HDF appeared twice under two names and a 0 MB stub was referenced; plans mixed 30 s and 1 s intervals
  and RAS 6.70 / 7.00 / 7.01; a test plan changed the Current Plan (DLR-001).
- The .rasmap projection came from a feature shapefile .prj; spot points were EPSG 6426 while rasters were EPSG 2230
  (a silent realization mismatch of up to a few ft) (DLR-002).
- A 53 GB base tif with VRT scenarios; stored maps referenced terrain clones not delivered; DEM tiles delivered twice
  including two 6.8 GB copies (DLR-003).
- Captions cited a plan and short ID that no plan file carried; 12 plans and 8 geometries made the wrong HDF easy to
  read (TANGERINE-004).
- 100-yr and 10-yr plans pointed to the same flow file; a sync conflict copy of a 225 MB geometry HDF; the same tiles in
  three terrain folders; about 60 geometry backups (SAHPARK-016).
- A folder named Alt1 held a channel and artificial barriers the preferred alternative did not have; both 500-yr
  folders were empty and the old 500-yr was 1.75 x Q100, not a run (NORTHLOOP-006).
- Lidar under water and bridge decks gives no channel bottom or low chord; expect high WSEL bias (CALFIRE-011).
- The agent first wanted a duplicate-effective baseline; JCO clarified the fixed-map intent (SILVERBELL-002).
- A trial over all 100 intersecting XS reported a spurious 23.7 ft surcharge from disconnected polygon pieces; the
  project reach gave about 4 ft existing surcharge and 0.16 ft rise; clipping floodway polygons before deriving
  boundaries broke the areas (SILVERBELL-002).
- Local-peak tributary runs with iterated tailwaters are not a mass-conserving network; a local model that differs
  from FEMA effective supports no no-rise or CLOMR finding; long runs need a checkpoint that supersedes old status
  (SILVERBELL-001).
- Scope asked for refuge to the 500-yr while the basis covered 10/100-yr only (client decision); an existing berm
  breaks out near the 10-yr (PHXZOO-002).
- Effective TDN listed 3-hr 3.34 in and 24-hr 4.55 in storms; only the 3-hr case was in the package and both the main
  package and blind rebuild ran 3-hr only; no flood envelope from one storm (STARVALLEY-022).
- Highlighter terms must match manual wording (USGS SIR 2012-5113 gave 4 hits on region terms) (CALFIRE-002).
- Town code text was readable online only as a table of contents; confirm with Town staff instead of assuming County
  criteria (PHXZOO-004).
- No published animal-facility drainage standard exists; state that topology as engineering judgment (PHXZOO-004).
- Keep research separate from minutes so unverified web findings stay OPEN (PHXZOO-004).
- Folder showed only desktop.ini until a manual download; a bulk upload created a nested 50 GB duplicate; OneDrive
  resets timestamps (TANGERINE-009).
- Upload grew from 1,726 to 2,653 files during review; correspondence did not show prior agency approval; the prior
  report stated Q500 two ways (NORTHLOOP-001).

## Stop conditions
- Jurisdiction not confirmed from a saved GIS response: stop; no criteria adopted.
- Inventory still growing (project-intake not final): findings stay provisional; do not issue.
- A governing document cannot be found: record as a request and OPEN; never substitute another agency's criterion.
- Scanned page unreadable after local OCR: record the page and request a better copy; never infer the value.
- EKOS-LOCAL job: do not fetch directly; write the retrieval script and queue it (D14).

## Escalation (to JCO)
- Jurisdiction or review-path questions (city vs state-coordinated review; which agency signs).
- Design basis choices: which study governs, events beyond the published set, D22 fallback for 500-yr WSE.
- Approved-vs-recalculated differences (storage, HW vs allowable).
- High-influence unverified assumptions before a draft issues; owner outlet assumptions.
- Criteria that change a prior approved study.

## Learning log
End every run with `log_lesson(project='<job no>', text='<source found or missing, where, what it changed>',
evidence=['<register or summary path>'], source_ai='<platform>')`, or on EKOS:
`D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe D:\EKOS\Library\09_Server\library_cli.py log-lesson --project <job no> --source-ai <platform> --text "..." --evidence "<path>"`.
New agency URLs, editions and request routes are lesson material; project facts are not.

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from clusters DSO-C01, DSO-C02, QC-C10, QC-C23, HYD-C13, HYD-C16, HJR-C08, HJR-C11,
  HJR-C22, DSO-C13; decisions D14, D22, D25, D55, D56. Items marked "default, to confirm": D55 (EPSG:2868 default for
  Pima County), D25 values (East Placer WQ depth and groundwater separation).

## Skill: project-intake v1.0.0

# Project Intake

## When to use
- Starting AI or script work on a project folder (often OneDrive), a new job, or an update of an earlier study to
  current standards that needs a short scope.
- A HEC-RAS or FLO-2D model set is received, or reused from an archive.
- Base GIS, terrain, record plans or reference documents must be assembled before hydrology or hydraulics.
- Incoming survey, CAD, LandXML or GIS must be checked against the model grid.
- The prior/adjacent study screen and jurisdiction confirmation that follow are run by `due-diligence-researcher`.

## Inputs
- Source project folder (read-only) and a work area on a local non-synced drive (D:).
- Job number, jurisdiction (to be confirmed), client ask.
- `%DOCS_PY%` / `%GIS_PY%` = documents and GIS venv interpreters by full path (D11); `%SK%` = this skill's `scripts\`.
- On EKOS-LOCAL jobs, data retrieval runs on the local worker from replayable scripts and saved configs (D14).

## Steps

### A. Real files, copy, inventory (DSO-C13)
1. Check the folder holds real files, not only desktop.ini or cloud placeholders. Set "Always keep on this device" or
   download first. `intake_inventory.py` flags cloud-only files, desktop.ini-only folders and empty folders.
2. After any bulk upload, check for a nested copy of the folder inside itself and for size growth before work starts
   (the inventory lists nested-copy suspects).
3. Copy to the work area and log it:
   `robocopy "<source>" "D:\<work>\<Job>\Source_<YYYYMMDD>" /S /E /MT:8 /R:1 /W:1 /LOG:"D:\<work>\<Job>\Intake_<YYYYMMDD>\robocopy_<YYYYMMDD>.log"`
   then verify count, bytes and a SHA-256 sample:
   `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\intake_inventory.py" verify --src "<source>" --dst "D:\<work>\<Job>\Source_<YYYYMMDD>"`
   Record in the project notes that the copy is complete. Source files stay read-only; work on copies.
4. Inventory the whole project folder (path, size, mtime, readable, cloud-only) to CSV; ZIP contents separately;
   keep the inventory and all generated work outside the source job folder:
   `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\intake_inventory.py" inventory --root "<source>" --out "D:\<work>\<Job>\Intake_<YYYYMMDD>\inventory_<YYYYMMDD_HHMM>.csv"`
5. If an upload is still running, save dated snapshots and a delta (`--previous <earlier csv>`); rerun when complete;
   mark findings provisional until the inventory shows no growth (`"final": true`). File dates on OneDrive are sync
   times, not work history: keep a dated log.

### B. Job layout (D56)
6. Set the Standard job layout at the job work root: 00_Admin, 01_Reference, 02_Data, 10_Record, 20_Working,
   30_Report, 40_QC, 50_Correspondence (issued sets in 30_Report/Issued); dates YYYYMMDD in every name. Drainage report deliverables
   get their report folder from `drainage-report-standard` (make_report_folder.py). Working sandboxes
   `20_Working\<Initials>_<YYYYMMDD>_<Topic>\`.

### C. What the project already has (DSO-C13)
7. Identify the prior report, native model folders, current site plan/CAD, survey, geotech report and correspondence;
   record which layout the prior report actually adopted.
8. Check correspondence early for prior agency approval of the old report (decides addendum vs full replacement
   report). Do not reuse prior-report tables without tracing them to calcs.
9. Download all current jurisdiction standards into `01_Reference\Agency\Standards_<YYYYMMDD>\` with a register
   (title, edition date, URL, current or historical) - `reference/public_gis_and_records.md` C.

### D. Received or archived model sets (HYD-C13)
10. Keep the delivered zip/archive untouched as the record copy; work on an extracted copy. Budget disk at 2-3x the
    zip size; never open multi-GB tif/HDF in a viewer - read .vrt and .rasmap as text.
11. Register the HEC-RAS set without opening RAS:
    `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\ras_plan_register.py" --prj <model.prj> --out <model folder>\_plan_register.csv --json <..>\Intake_<YYYYMMDD>\ras_findings.json`
    It reads the .prj (registered Geom, Unsteady, Plan files; as-received Current Plan - record it before any edit),
    each .p## (Plan Title, Short Identifier, Geom File, Flow File, Program Version, Computation Interval), compares
    with the files on disk and flags unregistered plans, entries without files, stray copies (renamed .hdf, .tmp.hdf,
    snapshot HDFs, Backup.p##, sync conflict copies), plans sharing a flow file under different storm titles and
    generic plan titles. Never treat stray copies as results. Fill the condition, terrain and status (live /
    superseded) columns and keep the register in the model folder.
12. Confirm each plan's flow file matches its title/storm; separate titles or clearly named plans for existing vs
    proposed; rename generic plan titles to condition-specific names (on a copy) before results are reported.
13. FLO-2D archives: register every native folder (build, grid, run time, terrain changes vs base, levee/barrier
    records); diff each alternative grid against the base; match folders to report figures; never select by folder
    name or newest timestamp; separate artificial levee barriers from real proposed grading.
14. Terrain packages: list Terrain folder sizes and each scenario .vrt source and cell size; scenario modifications
    live in the terrain HDF or geometry, not the tif; identify duplicate source tiles; check stored maps' Terrain
    name and StoredFilename and regenerate missing maps.
15. Open in the same or newer RAS version on a copy only (opening rewrites plan and geometry files); record versions;
    a 7.x set is not upgraded or mixed into 6.6 work without a logged decision (D02).
16. Run and store models on a local non-synced drive; copy only final plan results to the synced share; delete
    .tmp.hdf and unused plan results before archiving (on the working copy).
17. Every caption and table that uses results cites plan file, short ID and geometry (report-writer applies this).

### E. Public data, terrain, records, reference documents
18. Public GIS and hydrology data: `"%DOCS_PY%" "%SK%\rest_harvest.py" --config <harvest.json> --out <job>\02_Data\GIS_Public\<YYYYMMDD>`
    (envelope query with paging, GeoJSON per layer, GeoPackage per theme in the GIS venv, `_download_log.csv`; one
    dead service is logged and the pass continues). Layer list and rainfall/soils/land-cover rules:
    `reference/public_gis_and_records.md` A. Resolve every ERR row before hydrology starts.
19. Terrain: `reference/terrain_dem_build.md` - extent over all contributing watersheds, TNM item list, tiles chosen
    by acquisition collection and logged (D53), clip before mosaic, project CRS, m->ft, DEMs at 3 ft (3.28 ft for
    native 1 m) for hydraulics/grading, 10 ft for hydrology, 30 ft for large basins (D54), per-source cell counts for
    composites, vintage differencing.
20. Record plans and field books: `reference/public_gis_and_records.md` B (catalog queries, page budget, SHA-256 and
    magic bytes, OCR with orientation, strict utf-8, deterministic quotes, numbers checked on the page image, crossing
    details accepted only when spatially anchored).
21. Reference documents: `reference/public_gis_and_records.md` C (copy unaltered, hash, page-aware extraction, OCR only
    low-text PDFs, encrypted PDFs left pending, human decisions in a separate sheet).

### F. CRS, units, vertical datum and the data log (DSO-C05; D55)
22. Start `02_Data\<Job>_DataLog_<YYYYMMDD>.md` from `reference/data_log_template.md`. Project CRS by jurisdiction from
    the survey basis; Pima County default NAD83(HARN) Arizona Central, intl ft, EPSG:2868 (D55, default, to confirm).
    Record the realization of every layer; mixing realizations is flagged.
23. Do not trust declared EPSG/.prj metadata: compare at least 3 known points to the model grid for every incoming
    CAD/GIS/LandXML file and log the result.
24. Local site coordinates: apply the documented local-to-State Plane transform (translate, rotate, scale about the
    base point); preserve CAD arcs with a chord tolerance before transforming.
25. Find the vertical datum and benchmark note in the survey; if absent, request it and mark dependent elevations
    (pads, floors vs modeled WSE) provisional.
26. Reconcile units (metric survey vs ft plans) before any grid update.
27. LandXML: P order is northing, easting, elevation; interpolate on the original triangles, exclude invisible faces,
    no extrapolation across voids; update the grid from the original survey triangles, not a new triangulation.
28. Compare the new survey surface with the model grid/DEM (mean, std dev); list differences over 2 ft and explain them.
29. Received model sets: read RASProjectionFilename in the .rasmap, the SRS of each .vrt and each delivered .prj;
    confirm the same horizontal realization and units (e.g. EPSG:2230 vs 6426 in California) and vertical datum;
    record the CRS of each layer before any reprojection.

### G. Findings and scope (DSO-C13)
30. Write numbered findings (F01, F02 ...) with severity, evidence locator (report page, model file) and action, in
    `00_Admin\<Job>_Intake_Findings_<YYYYMMDD>.md`. Issue only after the inventory is final.
31. Write the scope as plain text: one page target, two pages max, no subtasks, with assumptions and exclusions; list
    conditional services (FEMA map revision, regional model rebuild, easement-driven redesign) separately.
32. Hand off to `due-diligence-researcher` (prior and adjacent studies, existing conditions, jurisdiction
    confirmation) with the inventory, data log, model registers and findings.

## Jurisdiction add-ons
- `addons/pima-county-rfcd.md`: lidar collections and composite rule, target CRS (D55).
- `addons/fema.md`: NFHL layer set, LOMR check, screening vs duplicate-effective wording.
- `addons/caltrans-california.md`: tenth-postmile points, AADT, dam inundation; California CRS realization check.
- `addons/city-of-tucson.md`: Maps and Records catalog and field books.
- Arizona jurisdictions with a county manual use the manual's rainfall and soils sources (`drainage-report-build`
  add-on of that agency).

## Gotchas
- The folder showed only desktop.ini until a manual download; the run stalled about 1 h (TANGERINE-009).
- A bulk upload created a full nested duplicate of the project folder inside itself (about 2,258 files, 50 GB),
  about 3 h to sync (TANGERINE-009).
- OneDrive resets file timestamps to the sync time, so file dates cannot be used to estimate work history; keep a
  dated log (TANGERINE-009).
- The upload grew from 1,726 to 2,653 files during the review; findings from the first snapshot had to be revised
  (NORTHLOOP-001).
- Correspondence did not show prior agency approval of the old report (NORTHLOOP-001).
- The prior report carried conflicting dates and tables (Q500 basis stated two ways); do not reuse tables without
  tracing to calcs (NORTHLOOP-001).
- Plan p01 (floodwall, existing event) existed on disk with a 1.5 GB result HDF and was cited in the delivered data
  dictionary, but was not registered in the .prj, so it did not appear in the RAS plan list; add the plan back through
  the .prj or open the .p01 directly (DLR-001).
- A stray renamed copy of a plan result HDF (p02 with extra letters appended) was the same size as the real one; easy
  to map the wrong file (DLR-001).
- RAS Mapper listed a 91% snapshot HDF as a results layer next to the completed run; check the layer name for Snapshot
  before mapping (DLR-001).
- One geometry HDF appeared twice in RAS Mapper under two names, and a stub geometry HDF (0 MB) was referenced but not
  in the .prj (DLR-001).
- Plans mixed 30 s and 1 s computation intervals and RAS 6.70 / 7.00 / 7.01 files; a test plan created after receipt
  changed the project Current Plan; record the as-received Current Plan before editing (DLR-001).
- The .rasmap projection was set from a feature shapefile .prj under Features rather than the Terrain Projection.prj;
  it matched, but this is fragile when features are replaced (DLR-002).
- Delivered spot elevation points were in NAD83(2011) CA zone 6 ftUS (EPSG:6426) while all sampled rasters were NAD83
  CA zone 6 ftUS (EPSG:2230); a silent realization mismatch of up to a few ft if a GIS transforms on the fly (DLR-002).
- The base terrain was one 53 GB tif at 0.615 ft cells (about 430,000 px square) plus a 2.2 GB terrain HDF; the three
  scenario terrains were VRTs over that same tif (DLR-003).
- Stored depth maps referenced terrain clone names that were not delivered and output folders that did not exist, so
  they would not display until recomputed (DLR-003).
- The same USGS and county DEM tiles were delivered twice in two Terrain subfolders, including two 6.8 GB county DEM
  copies (DLR-003).
- Report and figure captions cited existing conditions as Plan 12 / EX_<init>_LG, but p12 was titled Plan 12 with no
  short ID (geometry g08), the project notes named p09 EX_<init> as existing, and no plan carried EX_<init>_LG
  (TANGERINE-004).
- 12 plans and 8 geometries in one project with superseded iterations p01-p08 make the wrong HDF easy to read; confirm
  the plan before exporting rasters (TANGERINE-004).
- Plans p05 (100-yr) and p06 (10-yr) both pointed to flow file u02 - the 10-yr run either used 100-yr flows or the file
  was overwritten between runs; it matched a mislabeled-storm comment on the draft (SAHPARK-016).
- OneDrive sync created a conflict copy of the g04 geometry .hdf (225 MB) (SAHPARK-016).
- The same 8 USGS tiles were copied into three terrain folders (SAHPARK-016).
- About 40 geometry saves (g02) and 19 saves (g04) in Backup show heavy iteration on berm and road terrain
  (SAHPARK-016).
- A folder named Alt1 had an eastern channel and 2,120 ft of artificial barriers, while the report's preferred
  alternative left the east natural (NORTHLOOP-006).
- Both named 500-yr folders were empty; the old 500-yr used a 1.75 x Q100 multiplier, not a saved run (NORTHLOOP-006).
- The NHD MapServer timed out at 180 s, then returned empty JSON on retry (4 passes); fall back to the staged HU8
  shapefile zip from the TNM S3 bucket (CALFIRE-003).
- Shapefiles truncate field names over 10 characters; keep the GeoPackage as master (CALFIRE-003).
- Log failures instead of stopping the loop so one dead service does not cost the whole pass (CALFIRE-003).
- PFDS returns JavaScript text (result = values; quantiles = [...]), not JSON; parse the arrays (CALFIRE-005).
- Dual groups (B/D, C/D) and Not rated units (3-6%) need a stated rule before CN assignment (CALFIRE-005).
- Display-clipped polygons must not feed hydraulic encroachment logic (SILVERBELL-013).
- An updated local model plus mapped lines is a screening, not a duplicate-effective model (SILVERBELL-013).
- Tiles carry 2-3 overlapping vintages (2017, 2019, 2025) and duplicate NED entries; filter or the mosaic mixes
  surfaces (CALFIRE-004).
- Newest-published logic picked the older 2018 collection (published 2025) on several tiles; fixed with a
  collection-preference step and a DEM rebuild (RKN-002).
- The initial DEM extent did not cover the full offsite watersheds; extending it changed several CP inputs and forced
  PC-Hydro reruns (RKN-002).
- A 107-tile merged input built a 20 GB terrain tif; clip first (DLR-007).
- Street and wash network shapefiles ended up listed under Terrains in the .rasmap (DLR-007).
- The USGS 2021 10-ft DEM contributed 0 cells to the composite and the run continued without noticing (SAH-020).
- Large changes (30 to 80 ft mean over hundreds of ac) were mine tailings growth, which affects depression volumes and
  flow paths (SAH-020).
- 1.8 GB of raw tiles per site (CALFIRE-004).
- Culvert inverts read from lidar are estimates only; carry as open items until survey (CALFIRE-004).
- USGS 1 m tiles are NAD83 UTM 12N in meters; convert to ft and compare to survey before use (DLR-007, STARVALLEY-014).
- The DLR-007 terrain lessons come from a test project, not the received set (DLR-007).
- LandXML declared EPSG:2223 but was in local coordinates; watershed and parcel shapefiles likewise had State Plane .prj
  files with local coordinates (STARVALLEY-014).
- Old channel files sat about 50 ft off the true centerline (STARVALLEY-014).
- One CAD vertex differed by 100 ft and was excluded (STARVALLEY-014).
- Survey CAD had no datum or benchmark statement; pad elevation and WSE remain provisional (NORTHLOOP-019).
- An early Delaunay terrain was replaced by exact LandXML triangles (26,507 cells updated) (NORTHLOOP-019).
- DCR vertical datum unknown; EG vs FG differences are not earthwork depths (SILVERBELL-007).
- The first field-book search stopped at page 1 and called the target missing (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- Sideways scans gave zero OCR hits on all 26 pages until orientation was corrected (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- Default cp1252 decoding failed on utf-8 OCR text (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- Free-form model quotes: only 40 of 137 matched the source exactly (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- OCR misread 2698.20 as 2696.20 on one record; two monuments with the same elevation were different points
  (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- Plan titles naming roads do not geolocate a structure; candidate crossing details stayed unaccepted until spatially
  anchored (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- 8 datum/crossing retrieval tasks, 5 failed or empty (EKOS-LOCAL-013).
- A 715-file reference intake ran 5.3 h; 220 of 264 PDFs verified, 16 timeouts, 18 page-label failures, 8 zero-text
  (EKOS-LOCAL-023).
- A stdout warning on a successful extraction made the orchestrator mark failure; judge by exit code and output
  artifact (EKOS-LOCAL-023).
- OCR of map pages misread labels (EKOS-LOCAL-023).
- Qdrant 1.15.3 accepted but did not return collection metadata; verify the fingerprint in point payloads instead
  (EKOS-LOCAL-022).
- LM Studio rejected the json_object response format (HTTP 400) (EKOS-LOCAL-022, EKOS-LOCAL-005).
- Only a synthetic 5-page test passed retrieval qualification; real manuals are not yet qualified (EKOS-LOCAL-022).

## QC checks
- Pull rules: `get_qc_rules('crs')`, `get_qc_rules('existing-conditions')`, `get_qc_rules('model-runs')`, plus the
  jurisdiction tag.
- Inventory final (no growth since last snapshot) before findings are issued; copy verification log (count, bytes,
  hash sample) present (NORTHLOOP-001, TANGERINE-009).
- Every cited plan exists, is registered, carries a condition-specific title and matches the caption; plan flow file
  matches plan title/storm (HYD-C13).
- `_download_log.csv` has no unresolved ERR rows before hydrology starts; HSG rule for dual/not-rated units stated in
  the assumption log (DSO-C03).
- Per-source cell count in a composite (any source with 0 cells stops the run); nodata fraction 0 inside the
  contributing area; DEM extent covers every contributing watershed (DSO-C04).
- Known-point check (at least 3 points) logged for every incoming CAD/GIS/LandXML file; vertical datum and benchmark
  stated for every survey used to set an elevation, otherwise labelled provisional; survey vs grid difference table
  with differences over 2 ft explained (DSO-C05).
- Every number taken from a record checked against the page image; every quoted excerpt matches the source
  byte-for-byte (DSO-C06).
- Data log names the realization of every layer (D55) and the cell size of every DEM (D54).

## Change log
- 1.0.0 2026-10-22: built from clusters DSO-C13, DSO-C04, DSO-C03, DSO-C06, DSO-C05, DSO-C09 and the intake part of
  HYD-C13 (steps 1-10; step 11 citation rule handed to report-writer); decisions D53, D54, D55 (default, to confirm:
  Pima County EPSG:2868), D56, plus D02, D11, D14. Added scripts intake_inventory.py, ras_plan_register.py,
  rest_harvest.py (tested on sample folders, a synthetic RAS project and a local mock REST service; live public
  services were not reachable from the build container) and reference files for data log, terrain build, public GIS,
  records and reference documents.

## Skill: drainage-report-build v2.0.0

# Drainage Report Build

## When to use
Any drainage report, TM, DCR or memo build, and any revision from a JCO markup or agency comments. This skill is the entry
point: it sets the order of work and the rules every report must meet, then hands each task to the skill or agent that owns
it. Jurisdiction rules (from the add-on) override anything here; decisions D01-D57 override older rules.

Who does what:
| Task | Owner |
|---|---|
| Assembly chain (workbook -> assemble_report.py -> post-process -> Word export -> compiled PDF) | `drainage-report-standard` |
| Exhibit sheet standards (sizes, ramps, base content, FIRM marking, text size) | `drainage-report-exhibit-standards` |
| Scripted exhibit series | `scripted-exhibit-sheets` |
| Writing narrative and tables | agent `report-writer`, always paired with agent `qc-reviewer` |
| Independent review, submittal audit, blind rebuild | agent `qc-reviewer` |
| Exhibit review | agent `exhibit-reviewer` |
| Prior studies, criteria research, jurisdiction confirmation | agent `due-diligence-researcher` |
| Long model runs, queues, rerun-all gate | agent `model-run-supervisor` |
| PC-Hydro | `pchydro-hydrographs` |
| HEC-HMS | `hechms-headless` |
| HEC-RAS 2D | `hecras-2d-models`; result rasters `hecras-result-rasters` |
| FLO-2D | `flo2d-model-runs` |
| HY-8 culverts | `hy8-native-runs`; legacy calc reruns agent `legacy-calc-reproduction` |
| Storm drain SWMM / SSA | `swmm-ssa-storm-drain` |
| Existing vs proposed comparison, rise maps | `impact-comparison` |
| FEMA CLOMR / LOMR packages and AD responses | `fema-clomr-lomr` |
| Groundwater reinfiltration | `groundwater-reinfiltration-sizing` |
| Letter or technical memo format | `drainage-technical-memo` |
| Agency comment-response log | `agency-comment-response` |
| Project intake, terrain, CRS log | `project-intake` |
| CAD base reissue | `cad-base-update` |
| Delivery package | `delivery-package-build` |
| Closeout lessons | `project-harvest` |

## Inputs
- Job folder in the Standard v0.3 layout (D56): 00_Admin, 01_Reference, 02_Data, 10_Record, 20_Working, 30_Report, 40_QC,
  50_Correspondence (issued sets in 30_Report/Issued); dates YYYYMMDD. If the job is not in this layout, run `project-intake` first.
- Scope / contract, parcel record and plat case, current plan set, survey, geotech report.
- The Standard workbook for the report (00_Admin) when the job uses the Standard.
- Prior studies and effective FEMA data (from `due-diligence-researcher`).
- For revisions: the marked-up PDF (JCO or agency) and the current editable source.

## Steps

### 0. Start: jurisdiction, governing manuals, method selection
1. Confirm the jurisdiction and the reviewing agency from the parcel record, plat case, GIS jurisdiction layer and the
   contract before choosing any manual. Where City vs County or Town vs County is unclear, record both readings and ask
   JCO. Flag any conflict with the project description.
2. Load the add-on(s) for that jurisdiction (table under Jurisdiction add-ons). More than one can apply (for example
   town-of-marana + fema).
3. Cite the current edition of each governing manual from the add-on; never cite a superseded document; cite the current
   version of any redone prior study. Keep the governing policies and program guides in `01_Reference\Agency` for citation.
4. Use the agency report outline as the section list when the agency publishes one. Keep every section; where nothing
   applies write "Intentionally left blank" with the reason.
5. Method selection (write it into the design-basis section and the workbook Setup):
   - hydrology method by watershed size and jurisdiction (add-on method table);
   - rainfall source, statistic, return period and duration;
   - design events for each system type (only the jurisdiction design set; anything else is labelled a sensitivity);
   - hydraulic tools from the licensed set (D16): FHWA Hydraulic Toolbox, HY-8, Civil 3D hydraulic tools, HEC-RAS 6.6,
     HEC-HMS 4.13, FLO-2D, PC-Hydro. FlowMaster and CulvertMaster are legacy (default, to confirm).
   - tabulate concentration points with method, area and design Q.
6. If the scope adopts published regional or effective hydrology instead of new hydrology:
   - read the agency supersession memo first and confirm which study governs at the site (study limits);
   - take Q10 / Q100 from the governing tables and state which engine's results are used where several are tabulated;
   - for an effective FEMA study read the TDN storm list and controlling-storm statement and confirm the package holds the
     rainfall-runoff model and inputs for every storm case; request missing cases before modelling;
   - an event outside the published set (for example 500-yr) needs written client agreement to a ratio method or is scoped
     as added service;
   - apply the study's technical guidance (mesh size etc.) to any new model; represent existing flow splits (berm
     breakouts) rather than assuming containment.
7. Plan deficiencies: where the design differs from or falls short of the current plan set, list each item and ask JCO how
   to handle it (revise plans, note in report, alternative design). Never assume plan revisions.
8. Open the one internal QC open-items document for the report in 40_QC (D44). Every assumption, decision item and
   missing input goes there, not into the deliverable text.
9. For a markup revision:
   - read the markup page by page (Bluebeam annotations) and build a response-log row for every comment
     (`agency-comment-response`; status per D45: Addressed / Partial / Assumed / Not Addressed / Cannot Determine / Stale;
     disposition in a separate field: incorporated / superseded / no change);
   - copy the marked-up PDF to the 40_QC T3 review folder as `<Job>_<ReportID>_<Milestone>_<YYYYMMDD>_JCO-Markup.pdf`;
   - edit builder inputs first, then rebuild; never run stale downstream builders.

### 1. Design basis and discharge traceability
1. Define each storm used (regional and local, design and FEMA) once, in existing conditions. Use the qualifier with every
   reference ("10-yr regional", "100-yr local"); no synonyms.
2. Build a design discharge table: source (cross section, culvert record or CP id), location, Q10, Q100, governing
   duration, use (crossing vs parallel flow), method. Every Q in text, tables and captions matches it: one value, one
   qualifier, one source per flow.
3. Restate the design basis in the design section with the same wording and numbers. Keep the summary flow equal to the flow
   that sized the structure (approach flow is not crossing flow).
4. Check every map caption and table title against the storm of the values shown.
5. Allowable velocity is the velocity permitted over a lining or soil, not "the velocity of the soil".
6. Critical facilities (substation, BESS, utility, emergency facility) and any site needing a 500-yr WSE (D22):
   - confirm the critical-facility designation and requirement with the jurisdiction (improvements above the 500-yr WSE
     plus any freeboard from the add-on);
   - 500-yr WSE source, in this order: FIS 0.2% profile only where its cross sections bracket the site (annotate the profile
     with project extents and values used); else agency 500-yr hydrology; else a documented provisional value with agency
     agreement. A 1.75 x Q100 ordinate scaling is a labelled sensitivity only. Zone AO depth is not an elevation;
   - state the 500-yr source once; tabulate floor, pad and equipment elevations with datum and the controlling 100-yr and
     500-yr WSE;
   - add a FEMA floodplain section: effective zones, floodway, BFEs, how they constrain the design, and the consequence if
     existing ground is below the 500-yr WSE.
7. Rise and impact thresholds are cited from the governing agency or stakeholder per project (D29); no hard-coded 0.1 ft.
   Comparisons use `impact-comparison`.

### 2. Content rules
Watersheds and hydrology
1. Onsite watersheds end at the property line; omit offsite areas draining away; existing and proposed totals match to
   two decimals. Set the onsite boundary at the project boundary so pre vs post is shown there.
2. Areas not regraded are modelled on existing contours.
3. Nested areas: list each catchment with its parent; run a total-area unattenuated case once; never add upstream basin
   outflows or pipe catchment flows to it. Where detention is modelled, route the upstream outflow and add only the
   incremental downstream area. Load soils and attributes by the same catchment key as geometry; stop on mismatched keys.
4. Offsite areas near a storm drain: bring in the storm drain, manholes and inlets; include roadway and upstream
   subdivision areas tributary to it; state the inlet capture assumption; label upstream offsite infrastructure.
5. Watershed exhibits: boundaries follow visible ridge lines on shown topo; flow arrows agree with contours; Tc path shown;
   "flowline" where no stream exists (contour intervals per `drainage-report-exhibit-standards`, D42).
6. Tc = hydrology program value (PC-Hydro 5-min minimum); never call time to peak Tc; table values match native output.
7. Percent impervious and cover need a stated source (plans, independently labelled imagery meeting a set acceptance, or a
   named cover scenario S1/S2/S3). Classifier output is not field truth.
8. Basin outlets not surveyed: search as-builts and GIS pipe layers first; else ask the owner once and store the answer as
   a versioned scenario (source = owner); supersede explicitly, never overwrite; flag implausible derived slopes. Fallback
   with no invert data: pipe from lidar with 1 ft minimum cover tied to outfall ground.
9. Rainfall tables state source, statistic, return period and duration; runoff-coefficient columns headed with the symbol
   (for example Cw) and plain numbers.

Detention, first flush, infiltration
10. Give preliminary pre vs post peak Q and storage estimates even at concept level. Preliminary detention where PR > EX
    (2, 10, 100-yr): Vs = Vin,PR x (1 - Qex / Qpr), max of the three events; replace with a routed design at final.
11. Keep flood detention, first flush / water quality, sediment storage and harvesting separate, each with its own
    criteria and maintenance. Distributed (pod-level) detention gets a ledger per pod: allowable Q, required volume,
    phasing trigger, responsible entity. Name maintenance access and the responsible entity.
12. First flush retained below the outlet invert (raise the outlet inlet rather than regrade the basin); shallow first-flush
    areas up to 9 in deep where needed. Model outlets exactly as drawn.
13. Drawdown = retained depth / design infiltration rate with the standard factor of safety. Untested rate (D23): state the
    basis used and that field testing is required; the add-on sets the method (Pima: required-rate method; Placer: half
    NRCS rate with 0 in/hr sensitivity).
14. Flag basins in mapped riparian habitat and outfalls direct to a major wash (detention waiver candidates).
15. Maintenance / inspection plan only if the jurisdiction requires it; otherwise ask JCO.

Channels, culverts, streets
16. Constructed unlined earthen channels n = 0.025; natural channels from land cover with the source cited (D27). Tables
    show required depth (normal depth + required freeboard) vs provided, and the lining (earthen / unlined, concrete,
    shotcrete, riprap).
17. 2D Manning n: land-cover n for new, concept and master studies; uniform n only when extending an accepted model, stated
    in the report (D28).
18. Collector / diversion channels: size for the combined flow of all intercepted paths; check superelevation at each bend
    from radius; screen bank height with a conservative case (2 x normal depth or summed peaks); check transitions, lateral
    inflow and basin backwater. Where sediment load is high do not default to riprap; evaluate concrete or shotcrete;
    include sediment cleanout access. Where a collector returns flow to natural ground, provide a level spreader and compare
    existing vs proposed outlet split by domain exit.
19. Culverts: structure sizes from survey or as-builts (state the verified size, no discrepancy narrative); outlet velocity
    and protection per HEC-14 (at 9-13 fps a dumped riprap apron alone is not enough); inlet / outlet channel inverts at or
    below the box invert; cutoff walls for 100-yr scour plus long-term degradation; state the overtopping criterion with the
    margin achieved and check sensitivity to weir length; note sediment risk of perpendicular alignments.
20. Every quoted hydraulic result maps to a line of program output (Q, HW elevation, inlet vs outlet control, barrel length,
    slope, outlet velocity). A soffit or crown elevation is not computed headwater. Assumptions cite the same cross section
    that sized the structure.
21. Streets and inlets: state the design spread criterion, clogging factors used and design frequency in every inlet /
    scupper table; scuppers analysed in sump unless stated; ROW velocity check; apply clogging once (a two-grate sump with
    one grate assumed blocked already covers clogging); do not claim no bypass unless the calcs show it. Values per add-on.
22. Storm drain HGL: routing must be dynamic wave whenever HGL freeboard is reported; run fixed tailwater and free outfall
    cases and state the same boundary in model and text; compare peaks with receiving-system capacity and HGL before
    choosing retention vs discharge.

Narrative content (required in the first draft)
23. Project description: scope / RFP wording where the agency or client requires it (verbatim where the add-on says so);
    describe the improvement accurately (which part is developed, direction of expansion).
24. Existing conditions under one main heading with subheadings: area description (land use in every direction, slopes as
    range / average % and direction, soils); adjacent landowners and development (name the major adjacent owner); existing
    infrastructure (roads, berms, culverts, storm drains with sizes); existing hydrology, drainage easements, mapped local
    floodplains, existing basins. Split existing hydrology (offsite and onsite watersheds with calcs) from existing
    stormwater infrastructure.
25. Describe how the site drains today, including ponding locations, spill elevation and path, and ponding behind
    embankments; verify against topo.
26. Include the roadway typical section from the latest plan set; if uncurbed, say so and state that spread and inlet
    analyses do not apply. Delete statements about analyses not done (say why not needed) and template text for features
    the project does not have.
27. Floodplain status: FIRM summary (map number, panel, effective date, zones) for the project limits; effective and pending
    panels and which governs at submittal; read the zone at the actual alignment.
28. CP flows are stated as sums of sub-basins; one table compares calculated Q with prior-study Q for every CP, with
    differences discussed.
29. Describe the 2D model setup (culverts, cell size, refinement, inflows) before results; state which return periods and
    scenarios were run in each model (run matrix from completion files, not from the plan).
30. State whether increases reach habitable structures and give the cause.
31. Every exhibit citation gives figure number and appendix.
32. Terms: natural washes are "washes", engineered ones "channels"; no relative words ("near") - say "on the site" or
    "within the improvement limits". Short sentences and short paragraphs. No heading without body text.
33. Text started from another report: search for remnant road, wash, project names and old footers (target zero hits);
    update criteria to this project; verify claims about ditches, profile changes and ponding with the roadway team.
34. Concept reports: label concept level on the title page and executive summary; state what the report does not do (no
    entitlement, no new hydrology, no permitting) in the executive summary, the public-concern section and the conclusions;
    replace unearned compliance words with "is structured to meet, to be confirmed in the master drainage report"; keep
    objective findings separate from land-plan recommendations; state path continuity under major crossings and
    whether each existing structure stays, is adequate or is replaced; get written client decisions on level of protection
    and any designed overflow onto the site.
35. Criteria in minutes or text carry a citation or are marked OPEN in the QC open-items document; County criteria stay
    "County" until the Town confirms in writing.
36. Cite only real sources. Never mention superseded drafts, the calc workbook, Excel, scripts or independent checks.
    References numbered 1), 2), ... with online links where available.
37. Deliverables are written in completed tense; nothing reads as interim, draft or pending (D44).

### 3. Formatting
1. Build to this standard from the first draft (numbered sections and subsections, template styles for headings and
   spacing, no manual returns); do not build a generic layout and patch it later.
2. Page breaks only before main sections (1.0, 2.0 ...) and appendices; no half-empty pages, no orphaned headings, no blank
   areas
